account:
Today has mostly followed my ordinary appointments: market, lunch, town accounts, tea with my dockside neighbour, and afternoon office hours. But I have heard several odd hints without a clear explanation. Several townsfolk said the baker was carrying a sack of bread at the inn. That could simply be a delivery; I have not established its purpose. At tea, my neighbour reported talk of lights at the bakery, although the baker apparently knew of no celebration. The neighbour also traced a muddled rumour to Townsfolk 02 outside the bakery this morning: 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Others repeated it, but my neighbour saw no change, and I have no confirmed riverfront plans or explanation. I should not treat those repetitions as independent evidence.

The builder has invited me to inspect the great hall lighting tomorrow at 18:00. That is a definite planned activity, and the secretary has recorded it, but I do not know whether it relates to the bakery-light gossip. Perhaps there is some preparation or gathering behind these hints, but a celebration or coordinated scheme would only be speculation. I have not personally seen one.

The secretary came to the cottage seeking the town-account materials. I found 128 emeralds in the treasury, but no account papers; neither of us has established where the ledger and receipts are. That is unfinished administrative business rather than evidence of wrongdoing. Both appointment books are now back in the appointments chest, which I have just checked. I am in the office, and the innkeeper has approached within five blocks. They might have something to tell me, but have not spoken yet.
